visualChapters.label: Framed in Spring
visualChapters.title: Framed in Spring
visualChapters.description: A spring flower photographed through surrounding foliage. The leaves naturally frame the flower and isolate it as the main subject. Simple change in perspective turned an ordinary scene into an intentional composition.

images.description: A spring flower photographed through surrounding foliage. The leaves naturally frame the flower and isolate it as the main subject.

visualChapters.label: Orange in the Grass
visualChapters.title: Orange in the Grass
visualChapters.description: A minimal photograph of an orange lying in the green grass. The green and orange create a complementary color contrast. This exact photograph is also used in the website's wallpaper section.

images.description: A minimal photograph of an orange lying in the green grass. The green and orange create a complementary color contrast.

visualChapters.label: The Atmosphere
visualChapters.title: The Atmosphere
visualChapters.description: Warm, vibrant, film-inspired aesthetic inspired by Kodak Ultramax. Picnic blanket, playing cards, fruit, bubbles, oranges, green grass, spring flowers, natural sunlight — the Secret Garden gave exactly the environment needed.

images.description: Candid moments from the picnic — cards, fruit, conversation.
The Secret Garden at ASU — green grass, spring flowers, natural light.
Playing with bubbles in the spring sunlight.
Film cameras on the picnic blanket — the FPC aesthetic.
Oranges scattered on the grass beneath the orange tree.
Golden spring light filtering through the garden.

closingStory: Overall, this was a really fun shoot. I went into it wanting to create something with a strong film-inspired look, and this event ended up giving me exactly the kind of environment I needed. I'm really satisfied with how the photographs came together — and, more importantly, with how closely the final result matched the feeling I had in my head when I started.
websitePresentation: Feel like a visual story rather than a standard photography gallery. When an image is specifically referenced in the story, use that image near the relevant paragraph so the viewer can see the photograph while reading about the creative decision behind it. Use editorial image titles instead of filenames — titles should feel photographic and intentional rather than generic labels like 'Flower' or 'Orange'. Do not invent specific technical details. Story remains primary narrative, images act as visual punctuation. Do not make writing sound like a formal case study — preserve personal, reflective, conversational character.
